Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Work & responsibility

producer noun

of a play, a film or a show

also film producer, theatre producer, stage manager, impresario, produce a play

classical

Plaut. Pers. 1.3.79, Trin. 4.2.16, Curc. 4.1 (old numbering; Lewis & Short)
Traupman 169

chorāgus, chorāgī m.

noun, second declension

the producer, who supplies what a show needs

(vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

From Greek χορηγός, the citizen who paid for a chorus. In Plautus he is the man who hires out the costumes and props for a play, and in the Curculiō he steps on stage himself to fret about his costumes (Lewis & Short); Traupman gives the word for a producer. Lewis & Short also cites it, once, for the one who pays for a banquet (Suet. Aug. 70).

See also perform.

SourcesLewis & Short: choragus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 169, 365 (producer).
